passages.text: But one of you will say, “Must we then do whatever we did among idols?” I tell you: not everything, but whatever you did well, and here to a greater degree. For whatever is done well in error derives from the truth, just as if something is done badly in the truth, it comes from error. Therefore reclaim what is yours from everywhere, not what belongs to others, and do not say, “If those who have been deceived do something good, we ought not to do it.” For by this reasoning, if someone who reveres idols does not murder, we ought to murder because the person in error does not murder.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀπολάβετε οὖν ὑμῶν πανταχόθεν τὰ ἴδια, μὴ τὰ ἀλλότρια
lexical_decisions.chosen: Therefore reclaim what is yours from everywhere, not what belongs to others
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the ownership/reclamation metaphor, not a blanket rejection of practices also found outside the community.

passages.text: No: rather, do more, so that if those in error do not murder, we do not even become angry; if the person in error does not commit adultery, we do not even think of it in the first place; if the person in error loves the one who loves him, we also love those who hate us; if the person in error lends to those who have, we also lend to those who do not have. In short, we who hope to inherit the boundless age ought to do better than the good things done by those who know only the present age. We know that if their deeds, examined alongside our deeds on the day of judgment, are found equal in doing good, we too must be put to shame, while they, through error having done what is against them, must perish. I spoke of being put to shame in this respect: we did not do more than those of whom we also knew more. But if we are to be put to shame for displaying good deeds equal to theirs and not more, how much more if we display less good conduct than theirs?

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οἱ τὸν ἄπειρον αἰῶνα ἐλπίζοντες κληρονομεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: we who hope to inherit the boundless age
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἄπειρος means boundless or endless; αἰών remains age, contrasting the present age.

lexical_decisions.chosen: those of whom we also knew more
lexical_decisions.rationale: The comparative expresses greater knowledge and responsibility; knew more than they did is an alternative English expansion.

passages.text: That on the day of judgment the actions of those who have known the truth are indeed measured against the good deeds of those who have been deceived, the one who does not lie himself taught us ...., saying to those who neglected to come and listen to him, “The queen of the south will rise with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom; and look, something greater than Solomon is here, and you do not believe.” To those among the people who were unwilling to reorient at his proclamation, he said, “Men of Nineveh will rise with this generation and condemn it, because on hearing they reoriented in response to Jonah’s proclamation; and look, something greater ... is here, and no one believes.” Thus, setting over against each of their acts of impiety those from the nations who had acted, to condemn those in reverence toward God who had not done even as much good as those who had been deceived, he admonished those with understanding not merely to do good things equally with the nations, but to do more. My discourse flowed on, taking its starting point from the need to observe the menstrual period and to immerse oneself after intercourse: not to reject such purity even if those who have been deceived practice it, since those in error who do good serve to condemn those in reverence toward God, although they themselves are not saved. For their honoring of purity is because of error, not because of worship of the true Father and God of all.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the one who does not lie himself taught us ....
lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected edition has four gap dots; exactly four remain, without reconstruction.

lexical_decisions.chosen: and look, something greater ... is here
lexical_decisions.rationale: Exactly three gap dots remain. No familiar proper name from another witness is supplied.

lexical_decisions.chosen: they reoriented in response to Jonah’s proclamation
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses POB reorientation terminology, traditionally repented, preserving the stated occasion of the response.

lexical_decisions.chosen: although they themselves are not saved
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the author’s explicit non-salvation claim about people in error who nonetheless do good.

passages.text: After saying this, he dismissed the crowds and, as usual, shared salt with his closest friends and rested. By acting and discoursing in this way, on each occasion he brought people securely to God’s law, exposing the supposed ones along with the supposed destiny, and showing that there is no spontaneity, but the world is governed according to providence.

lexical_decisions.chosen: shared salt with his closest friends
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains salt-sharing rather than merely an unspecified meal.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοὺς νομιζομένους μετὰ τῆς νομιζομένης γενέσεως
lexical_decisions.chosen: the supposed ones along with the supposed destiny
lexical_decisions.rationale: The masculine plural has no expressed noun, contextually the supposed gods. γένεσις can be birth or natal destiny; destiny fits the contrast with providence, with natal fate or horoscope as more specific alternatives.
Spontaneous or chance occurrence; chance is a viable more idiomatic alternative.

passages.text: When three months had been completed, he instructed me to fast for days, led me to the nearby springs in the sea, and baptized me in water as ever-flowing water. After our brothers had thus feasted at my God-given rebirth, not many days later he turned to the elders before the whole assembly and gave these instructions: “Our Lord and prophet, who sent us, explained to us how the evil one conversed with him for forty days and, having gained no power against him, promised to send apostles from among his own subjects to deceive. Therefore, above all, remember not to ... an apostle or teacher or prophet before he has compared his proclamation with James, who is called the brother of my Lord and has been entrusted in Jerusalem with administering the assembly of the Hebrews, and has come to you with witnesses. This is so that the evil that conversed with the Lord for forty days and gained no power, and afterward fell like lightning from heaven to earth, may not send out a herald against you, as it has now put Simon in our way, proclaiming in the name of your Lord under the pretext of truth, but sowing error. For this reason the one who sent us said, ‘Many will come to me in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves; recognize them by their fruits.’”

lexical_decisions.chosen: he instructed me to fast for days
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied wording gives days but no explicit number; none is restored.

lexical_decisions.chosen: baptized me in water as ever-flowing water
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves ὡς and the ever-flowing quality instead of dropping the qualification.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μὴ πρότερον . . . ἀντιβάλλοντα αὐτοῦ τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰακώβῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: not to ... an apostle or teacher or prophet before he has compared his proclamation with James
lexical_decisions.rationale: Exactly three dots remain. The governing action is unavailable and is not supplied as receive or trust. The negative/before relation, comparison of proclamation, and subsequent witnesses remain.
Keeps my here and your Lord later rather than harmonizing pronouns.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Many will come to me in sheep’s clothing
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the supplied to me, rather than importing a familiar to you from another witness.
